| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Disorders are causal loops, not latent causes | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. The convergence is real; the evidence is indirect, simulated or clinical, and none of it is an individual time series showing hysteresis, so the account is Proposed. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-061](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-061.md) | Goals set accumulation parameters, not responses | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) define cognitive control, in a two-choice task, as the adjustment of drift, starting point and threshold to maximise a utility. Ratcliff and McKoon ([LIT-576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-576.md)) find that the manipulations behave that way: speed or accuracy instructions are fitted by boundary separation alone, stimulus proportions mainly by starting point, difficulty by drift alone. Schurger et al. ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) carry the picture to the decision of when to move: the task goal raises the baseline toward threshold and leaves the moment to fluctuation. The convergence is real; the evidence is group fits on a few paradigms, so Proposed. It does not say who sets the parameters, or how. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-074](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-074.md) | Self-reports miss implicit true-self accessibility | Schlegel, Hicks, Arndt & King (2009), [LIT-606](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-606.md): true-self accessibility, the speed of "me" judgments for traits a person takes to be her true self, correlated .05 with AI-3 authenticity and .20 with basic need satisfaction (N = 124), and each predicted meaning in life independently. The authors read this as showing the constructs differ, and concede the difference is confounded with method, reaction time against self-report. The two self-reports correlated .52, and felt autonomy was only one third of the need-satisfaction composite, whose autonomy items include "I can pretty much be myself". So the paper separates the implicit measure from both self-reports, and does not separate authenticity from autonomy. Proposed: one sample for the correlations, method unresolved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-475](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-475.md) | Hierarchical Bayes recovers DDM parameters best | Wiecki, Sofer & Frank (2013), [LIT-563](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-563.md), read in [NOTE-466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-466.md). Experiment 1 gives the lowest trimmed recovery error for HB on every parameter, and HB beat ML on the same data sets in every condition. Experiments 2–3 report more power to detect drift differences and trial-wise covariate effects, but HB was judged by a posterior-interval test and the others by t-tests, and the clean comparison was omitted. All data were generated from DDMs, with sz = st = 0. It is the standard partial-pooling result shown for one model family, not a test of the DDM. | Active |
| [THEORY-505](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-505.md) | Cooperation domains factor only by relevance | Curry, Jones Chesters & Van Lissa (2019), [LIT-496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md), read in [NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md), and the independent Turkish validation by Yilmaz, Harma & Doğruyol (2021), [LIT-513](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-513.md) ([NOTE-397](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-397.md)). Relevance items fit seven factors in all three samples (CFI .98 UK, .95 Turkey). Judgement items do not (CFI .87, .83), and a seven-domain model of both fails (CFI .73, .75). The items were written from the theory and selected for fit within each domain, several subscales correlate above .8, and no item is non-cooperative. This is evidence about the instrument's structure, not about what morality contains. | Active |
| [THEORY-613](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md) | MFQ-2's six foundations fit across 19 nations | Atari, Haidt, Graham, Koleva, Stevens & Dehghani (2023), [LIT-500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md), read in [NOTE-398](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-398.md). 36 items, developed in 25 populations, fit six factors in 19 nations (ESEM CFI .979). | [THEORY-766](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md) v3 | Rubber hand reports may reflect expectation | Botvinick & Cohen (1998) and four replications read here give a synchrony effect on reports of referred touch and ownership. Rohde et al. (2011) and Abdulkarim & Ehrsson (2016) separate drift from ownership. The suggestion debate (Lush 2020; Lush et al. 2020; Ehrsson et al. 2022; Lush & Seth 2022; Roseboom & Lush 2022) shows that the standard controls do not equalise expectations. The ownership report is weaker than the referred-touch report and tracks trait suggestibility. Whether the synchronous stimulation, not expectation, produces the report difference is not settled. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the report differences measured ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3); the perceptual reading is [THEORY-827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-827.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-892](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-892.md) v2 | Psychopathy is one dimension, not a type | Hare and Neumann (2008), read in [NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md). The PCL-R's twenty items load on four correlated factors, which pair into Factor 1 (interpersonal, affective) and Factor 2 (lifestyle, antisocial) and are explained by one superordinate factor. The affective features are tied to the antisocial ones, so the authors deny that any component is the disorder's core, and they read the evidence as dimensional. Filed for the record's question on corporate psychopathy, which asks which of these features could be said of a corporation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1148.md) | Judges agree moderately on pragmatic similarity | Ward and Marco (2024), [LIT-1812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1812.md), read in [NOTE-1338](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1338.md) from the LREC-COLING 2024 PDF. Over 693 seed/re-enactment pairs in three sessions, mean pairwise Pearson agreement was 0.45, 0.72 and 0.66 (Table 2), and 0.80 in Session 2 when lexically different pairs were left out (p. 160). The Spearman–Brown reliability of the panel means, 0.88–0.96, is my computation. The judges talked during the session and knew each other, and all pairs are within one language, so the figure is neither a floor for a panel nor a value for translations. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1424](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1424.md) v2 | Motor skills decay roughly linearly with disuse | Tatel (2023), [LIT-2079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2079.md), the PhD dissertation behind Tatel & Ackerman (2025), [LIT-2088](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2088.md); read in NOTE-1560. A random-effects meta-regression over 457 sources. The slopes are the article abstract's too; the half-loss ranges are the dissertation's (the article gives 6.5, 13 and 11 months). The practice moderator holds for accuracy only, and the author calls the moderators far from definitive. It does not say that decay is linear beyond a year, where data are few, or anything about organizations. Active as a report of one meta-analysis; whether an independent synthesis agrees is open. | Active |

| [THEORY-2211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2211.md) | Lab motor skills decay faster than real ones | Tatel (2023), [LIT-2079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2079.md), and the coded data posted for Tatel & Ackerman (2025), [LIT-3080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3080.md). For accuracy the decline is 0.16 SD a month on laboratory tasks and about 0.05 on real-world tasks; the dissertation finds "less evidence" that real-world domains differ from one another, and in the posted data medical and dental tasks decline by 0.04 a month while sports and military or transport tasks show no measurable decline over intervals of a year at most. Speed shows the same trend, not significant. Task type is confounded with complexity and with the range of intervals studied. Proposed: one synthesis, by the same author, and the article unread. | Proposed |
